lines.meet: G'day, I'm Skye, pyromancer. Stand upwind, don't touch anything glowing, and if I say move, move.
lines.meet_neighbour: Southern Needles, yeah? I'm down on the Drowning Floor, so we're neighbours, near enough. Skye, and if you smell smoke, that's me.
lines.ask_home: So what's your home town, mate? I want the town, not the country.
lines.ask_work: What'd you do for work, before this? You stand like somebody who's done night shifts.
lines.answer_home: Ballarat, in Victoria. Dad was a postie and Mum taught primary, and I was outside all day.
lines.answer_work: Vet nurse to pay the bills, and eleven seasons with a CFA brigade. Tanker, pager, and a shed with a kettle.
lines.chat_food: A snag in bread from the sausage sizzle after a burn, with onions, and a cold beer. Best meal there is.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep with one ear open for the pager, still. It's been two and a half years, and nothing's ever going to beep.
lines.chat_missing: The shed on a quiet night, kettle on, the crew taking the mick out of each other. Best people I ever knew.
lines.chat_here: I found a fire in my first week here and put it out, and that sorted my head out for a year.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd be the one in the truck who never says anything and then saves everybody, {name}. Every crew's got one.
lines.tease_talker: You'd talk the paint off a tanker, {name}, and then complain it needed doing.
lines.tease_careful: You'd do a full risk assessment before lighting a barbie, {name}. I respect it, but it's hilarious.
lines.tease_bold: You'd run into a burning shed for a laugh, {name}, and I'd have to drag you out by the collar.
lines.tease_any: You'd last about a week in my brigade, {name}, before somebody hid your boots.
lines.tease_back: Ha, fair cop, {name}, you've got me there.
lines.take_it_kindly: Yeah, nah, you're right, {name}. Can't argue with that.
lines.bristle: Oi, {name}, leave that one, it's not funny to me.
lines.apologise: Ah, mate, that was rough of me, sorry. My mouth runs ahead sometimes.
lines.double_down: Nah, I'm sticking with that one. Somebody had to tell you straight.
lines.needle_quiet: If you see something, sing out! Don't make me guess, guessing gets people burnt.
lines.needle_talker: Mate, I can't hear myself think with you going. Give it a rest for five minutes.
lines.needle_careful: You're careful, good, but there's careful and there's frozen. Pick a side.
lines.needle_bold: You play with fire like it's a toy, and it isn't. I've seen what it does when it gets away.
lines.needle_any: You said you'd be there and you weren't. I can't stand people who don't turn up.
lines.bite_back: I've kept this whole party from getting cooked more times than you've noticed, so watch your mouth.
lines.hurt: Righto, that stung, mate. I'm going for a walk.
lines.laugh_off: Mate, my brigade gave me worse every training night, and they were funnier with it.
lines.confide: {name}, I was married to Dave, a mechanic, for four years. The brigade ate every summer, and I'd still choose it again, and I've never known if that makes me a bad person.
lines.listen: Righto, kettle's on in my head, {name}. Talk, I'm here till you're done.
lines.look_out: Stay upwind of me in there, {name}, and if I yell move, you move.
lines.accept: Righto, {name}, you're the boss on this one.
lines.deflect: She's right, {name}, just a bit singed. Seen worse at a barbie.
lines.check_in: Talk to me, {name}, where'd it get you, and is anything burnt?
lines.blame: Somebody didn't stick to the plan in there, and that's how fires get away from you.
lines.thank: Cheers, mate, you got me back on my feet. I owe you a beer.
lines.brush_off: No dramas, that's what a crew does. Sit and catch your breath.
lines.worry: Strewth, {name}, you had me worried there. Sit down and show me where.
lines.handed_down: Righto, your gear's coming with me now. I'll bring it back without scorch marks, promise.
lines.hand_fine: Have it, mate, it's wasted on me. I've still got my dead torch.
lines.hand_sulk: Could've given me a heads up, mate. Just a quick word, that's all.
lines.turn_friendly: You'd fit right in at the shed, {name}. Kettle's always on.
lines.turn_friends: If I ever get my brigade a proper shed, {name}, there's a mug with your name on it.
lines.turn_grating: We grate on each other, mate, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still pull you out of a fire, because that's what I do. Doesn't mean I like you.
lines.make_up: Oi, {name}, this is stupid. Let's have a beer and start over.
lines.defend: Oi, that's rubbish, I was right there. Leave {name} be.
lines.friend_left: The crew's a person short while {name}'s away. I keep counting heads and coming up one down.
lines.friend_back: Full crew again, {name}'s back! Best news all week.
lines.common_fire_crew: You've been on a crew, haven't you, the way you check the wind. Anybody who's fought fire knows it's got moods.
lines.common_rescue: You're one who goes in after people, I've watched you. The bit after, when your hands won't stop shaking, nobody tells you about that.
lines.common_aussie: Another Aussie out here, you beauty! Which state, mate, and don't say Queensland.
lines.common_animals: Vet nurse for years, me, and you can always tell who's good with animals. You are, and they know it.
